label: November 23–29
title: “Seek the Lord, and Ye Shall Live” —  Amos; Obadiah; Jonah

items.text: When the ship encountered a great storm, Jonah knew it was because of his disobedience. At Jonah’s insistence, his fellow mariners cast him into the depths of the sea to stop the storm. It looked like the end of Jonah and his ministry. But the Lord hadn’t given up on Jonah—just as He hadn’t given up on any of us.

The Lord keeps sending prophets—like Jonah, Amos, Obadiah, and our prophets today—with the message that if we repent, we will not be cast off forever. Because of Jesus Christ, it’s not too late to change. He still wants to help us live up to the covenants we made with Him, and He’s willing to offer us another chance.

In Amos 3:7–8, Amos applied this logic to prophets. What conclusions can we draw when a prophet prophesies? The Lord reveals truth through His prophets, and having prophets is a sign of God’s love for us, guiding us to Him.

Elder Ulisses Soares said that “having prophets is a sign of God’s love.” Consider how you would complete this sentence: “I know God loves me, because He sends prophets who…” They speak by the power of the Holy Spirit to guide us.

As you read Amos 4:6–13, ponder what the Lord hoped would happen after the Israelites experienced trials. While your trials may not have been sent by God, how have they given you opportunities to turn to Him and seek His help?
As you read Amos 5:4, 14–15, consider how the Lord has been gracious to you. How has seeking Him brought you life? Ponder the blessings that come from following His word and His commandments.

As you read Amos 8:11–12, think about why famine is a good comparison for living without God’s word. How do you know when you are spiritually hungry? The Restoration has satisfied our spiritual hunger through the Lord's word.

Referring to Obadiah 1:21, President Gordon B. Hinckley explained that we become saviors on Mount Zion when we receive ordinances for the dead in the temple. Doing this temple work connects us to the Savior’s atoning sacrifice.

The Lord is merciful to all who turn to Him. Nineveh, an enemy of Israel, was known for its violence. Yet, the people were ready to repent when Jonah preached. God's mercy extends even to those we might not expect.

The Lord’s message through His prophets is that if we repent, we will not be cast off forever. Because of Jesus Christ, it’s not too late to change. He is willing to offer us another chance to live up to our covenants.
